clue.text: Take down a French exercise, grudgingly at first

parts.note: the French word for 'a'
PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: what comes at first is the opening letter, so only the start of grudgingly is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone reluctantly writes down a French exercise at school.
explanation.walkthrough: UN is French for 'a', a favourite crossword borrowing.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpeg washing or a tent is to remove its pegs and so take it down from where it hangs.

clue.text: Not satisfactory to cancel pub tea randomly

indicators.note: letters put in a random order are jumbled, so the phrase before it is rearranged

parts.note: the twelve letters as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that calling off the pub's afternoon tea on a whim is poor form.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unacceptable falls short of the required standard, which is exactly what failing to satisfy means.

clue.text: Makes an announcement in favour of demand by son

parts.note: pro means for, supporting
to claim is to demand as a right
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent publicly supports a son's demand.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim is to declare something publicly and formally, a plain synonym for announcing it.

clue.text: Prepare good meal in a flash

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good

indicators.note: to prepare food is to work it into a new form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: Cooking a decent dinner very quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a flash' reads as 'quickly', but only 'flash' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a brief shining of light, the same as a momentary flash.

clue.text: Extremely desirable to stop involving resistance in drop

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters, so only those of desirable are kept

parts.note: its first and last letters

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: to cease is to stop
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Wanting a halt to any opposition to a fall in numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop' looks like an instruction, but it is the word that takes in the resistance symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A decrease is a reduction or fall, so it means a drop as a noun.

clue.text: Certainly have fewer qualms

definitions.meaning: second meaning: split as two words, to have less uncertainty

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning works only when the answer is read as two words, a verb and 'less'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubtless is an adverb meaning surely or undoubtedly; as 'doubt less' it describes being less hesitant.

clue.text: Manage to retire a period of years after losing husband

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, and in a down clue that sends the word upwards
losing something means it is taken away, so a letter drops out

parts.note: an epoch is an era, a long span of years
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone recently widowed tries to manage a retirement lasting years.
explanation.walkthrough: EPOCH turned round is HCOPE; take away the H and four letters are left.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to deal successfully with difficulties, which is what it means to manage.

clue.text: Regularly seen to oppose meeting

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of seen is kept

parts.note: its second and fourth letters
to counter is to oppose or act against

explanation.surface: Someone is often observed resisting a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: An encounter is a meeting, especially an unexpected one, so the noun is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Content to abolish outdated way of showing anger

indicators.note: the content of something is what it holds inside, so the letters sit within the phrase

parts.note: found running across the two words

explanation.surface: A campaigner happy to scrap an old-fashioned means of venting fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' reads as 'happy'; it means what is contained.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising one's voice loudly is a common outward expression of rage, so a shout shows anger.

clue.text: No abusive cop is possibly beyond reproach

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several possible arrangements of the letters before it

parts.note: the fourteen letters as written

explanation.surface: A police officer who never mistreats anyone may be blameless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like a link word but belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone above suspicion is so honest that nobody could reasonably doubt them, the same as being blameless.

clue.text: We will teach daughter to be knowledgeable

parts.note: taken as written
the contracted form 'll, as in we'll
to educate is to teach
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Parents promise to school their girl so she learns plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: WE plus 'LL together make we'll, the contraction of we will.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-educated person has had thorough schooling and so has wide learning and information.

clue.text: Jane could be a disaster

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer: Calamity Jane, the Wild West frontierswoman
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the nickname of the American frontierswoman ... Jane

explanation.walkthrough: Calamity Jane was a real Wild West figure, made famous by a Doris Day musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is a terrible event causing great damage, a catastrophe; it is also Jane's famous nickname.

clue.text: Whisper mistaken result

indicators.note: something mistaken is wrong, so the following word comes out in the wrong order

parts.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A rumour going round that an outcome was wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustle is a soft, dry murmuring sound, like leaves; a whisper is a similarly soft sound.

clue.text: Gripe terribly about loathsome advantage enjoyed by some

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the next word
done terribly means done badly, so the word before it is mangled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
vile means loathsome or disgusting

explanation.surface: A bitter complaint about an unfair edge some people have.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged complaint is split in two so that the loathsome word sits in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A privilege is a special right or benefit granted only to a particular group of people.

clue.text: I agree to cover the doctor to make up for it

indicators.note: covering something means going over and around it, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: taken as written
to nod is to show agreement
taken as written
MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: Someone volunteers to stand in for the GP to compensate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make up for it' looks like the definition, but 'make' is only a link and 'up for it' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the mood means feeling willing or inclined, the same as being up for something.

clue.text: Polite expression for you being against heartless feminism, we hear

indicators.note: without its heart, the central letters of the word are taken out

parts.note: taken as written
the word with its central two letters removed

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the result is judged by how it is said

parts.note: the two pieces said together

explanation.surface: Someone politely voices opposition to a movement, in a pun-laden way.
explanation.walkthrough: Feminism loses its middle IN; said after 'you', it sounds like the answer. 'Being against' just places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism is a mild or indirect word used in place of one considered harsh or blunt.

clue.text: Hearing test

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a case heard in court
second meaning: a trying out of something

explanation.walkthrough: Together the words suggest an ear examination, but they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A court case examining evidence is a judicial proceeding, and an experiment to see whether something works is also one.

clue.text: Be nosy about setter working rent free

indicators.note: letters that are working are moving about, so they get rearranged

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I
the letters as written

explanation.surface: A tenant living without charge is curious about the crossword compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: To interfere is to meddle in others' affairs, the prying behaviour of a nosy person.

clue.text: It's worth having in the manner arranged

parts.note: as means in the way that
set means placed or arranged

explanation.surface: A remark that something's value lies in how it is laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful or valuable thing or quality, something it pays to possess.

clue.text: Isolated copies retrospectively valued

indicators.note: looking back in time suggests reading backwards, so the word before it runs the other way

parts.note: to ape is to copy or imitate
rated means assessed or valued

explanation.surface: Duplicates given a price after the event.
explanation.definitionFit: Separated things are set apart from others, so they are cut off or isolated.

clue.text: Safely secure the ends of weedkiller in cupboard

parts.note: to lock is to fasten securely

indicators.note: the ends of a word are its closing letters, here the final pair

parts.note: its last two letters

explanation.surface: Advice to keep garden poison locked away in a cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: A locker is a small lockable storage compartment, such as one at a gym or school, a kind of cupboard.

clue.text: Series of recurrent low-level cyclones

indicators.note: recurrent suggests running back, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: found across the end of level and the start of cyclones

explanation.surface: Meteorology: a run of storms that keep returning close to the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run backwards across 'level cyclones'. 'Series of recurrent' looks like the definition, but 'recurrent' is working.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle is a sequence of events repeated in the same order, so it is a kind of series.

clue.text: Came across man touring Ohio for shooting

parts.note: to come across someone is to meet them

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a man's name
O is a short abbreviation for the US state of Ohio

explanation.surface: A traveller met someone on a road trip through Ohio who was going hunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' looks like hunting, but it is the shooting of a star.
explanation.definitionFit: Meteoric describes something like a meteor or shooting star: fast, bright and brief, as in a meteoric rise.

clue.text: Distinctive character of the crazily shaved boss

indicators.note: acting crazily means wildly, so the word before it is jumbled
shaving trims off the edges, so the outer letters of the word are removed

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
trimmed at both ends

explanation.surface: The personality of a manager who has gone mad with a razor.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit or set of values of a person, group or culture.

clue.text: Old friend can be precious

definitions.note: an adjective for a noun answer: an opal is a precious stone

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A long-standing friend is someone to treasure.
explanation.definitionFit: The opal is a gemstone prized for its play of colours, so it is something counted as precious.

clue.text: Achievement to keep quiet during a Conservative eulogy

indicators.note: during means in the course of, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a eulogy is high praise
sh is the instruction to be quiet

explanation.surface: A politician hushes up during a tribute paid to a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: The hush goes inside the praise word, not inside the Conservative abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An accomplishment is something successfully done, a feat, so it is a straight synonym for achievement.

clue.text: It's sleep-inducing to write note on 40% of curriculum

parts.note: to pen is to write
D is a note of the musical scale

indicators.note: forty per cent of a ten-letter word is four letters, here taken from its end

parts.note: its final four of ten letters

explanation.surface: A teacher complains that writing about a chunk of the syllabus is boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sleep-inducing' suggests something dull, but it is the hypnotist's swinging weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypnotist traditionally swings a pendulum or watch before a subject's eyes to put them into a trance.

clue.text: Pay out odds on final

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds when a race begins
the end is the final part

explanation.surface: A bookmaker settles bets made on a cup final.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, starting price, is a British betting term for the odds on a horse at the off.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend money is to hand it over in payment, so it is the same as paying out.
